planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained soil in full sun; strong stems hold the upright flame-shaped panicles without flopping even after rain.

directions: Grow in moist, well-drained soil in full sun for the heaviest bloom and strongest stem rigidity. This panicle hydrangea opens creamy white in midsummer and the florets gradually blush to deep rose-red by fall, giving two distinct color phases on the same plant. Because it flowers on new wood, prune hard in late winter if size control is needed without sacrificing the coming season's blooms. Established plants tolerate summer heat and occasional drought better than mophead hydrangeas.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in moist, well-drained soil in full sun; its 2-3 foot mature size suits containers and the front of a border where larger panicle hydrangeas would overwhelm the space.

directions: A true dwarf panicle hydrangea bred to stay under three feet, Flare still produces full-size conical flower clusters that open white and age through pink to a deep brick red by autumn. Plant in moist, well-drained soil in full sun; the compact habit means little to no pruning is needed to keep it in scale. Good as a repeating accent along a walkway or in large patio containers, and the aging flower heads hold color well when cut for arrangements.

common_name: Federico Garcia Lorca Lilac (Color-Shifting Double-Flowered Lilac)

planting.note: Plant container or bare-root shrubs in early spring or fall in well-drained, near-neutral soil in full sun; named for the Spanish poet, it needs real winter chill to bloom well.

directions: Plant in full sun with good air circulation in well-drained, near-neutral soil. This French lilac selection is notable for double trusses that visibly shift tone as each floret ages, cycling through blue, violet, lilac, pink, and magenta on the same panicle rather than opening a single fixed color. Remove faded flower clusters promptly after bloom since next year's buds set soon afterward, and thin a few of the oldest canes at the base every few years to keep flowering on vigorous younger wood.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in well-drained to moist soil in full sun for the brightest foliage color progression.

directions: New leaves emerge a vivid citrus-orange, age through yellow and green over the season, and finish fall in deep red and maroon tones, giving this tough native shrub three distinct color phases per year. Plant in well-drained to moist soil in full sun, which intensifies the color shifts; shadier spots mute the effect. Like other ninebarks it tolerates clay, heat, and short dry spells once established, and exfoliating bark on mature stems adds winter interest. Thin out the oldest stems at the base every two to three years to keep new colorful growth coming.

common_name: Birthday Cake Butterfly Bush (Sterile Narrow-Upright Buddleja)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in well-drained, lean to moderately fertile soil in full sun; the narrow upright habit fits tight borders and large containers better than wide-spreading older buddleja.

directions: Bred to be seed-sterile, this narrow, upright butterfly bush produces magenta-purple flower spikes through the growing season without setting viable seed, so it stays where it's planted and won't escape into wild areas the way older cultivars can. Plant in well-drained, lean soil in full sun; it tolerates heat and poor soil once established and draws butterflies and other pollinators reliably all summer. Cut stems back hard in late winter to encourage the strongest rebloom on new wood, and deadhead spent spikes periodically to extend flowering.

common_name: Prima Belarina Spring Sun Double Primrose (Fragrant Yellow Double Primrose)

planting.note: Plant container divisions in early spring in consistently moist, humus-rich soil in partial shade; shallow roots dry out quickly, so keep soil evenly moist through bloom.

directions: This compact double primrose carries lightly fragrant, fully double yellow flowers over a neat mounding rosette, blooming unusually early and over a long season for a primrose. Plant in consistently moist, humus-rich soil in partial shade; its shallow root system cannot tolerate drying out, so mulch and water during any dry spells. Expect the plant to go dormant in hot, dry summer conditions unless kept well-watered, then flush with new growth again as weather cools. Good for containers, shaded borders, and edging where early-season color is wanted.

common_name: Ever After Blush Reblooming Azalea (Double Soft-Pink Reblooming Azalea)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained, acidic soil in partial to full sun with at least five hours of direct light for best repeat bloom.

directions: A compact, semi-evergreen reblooming azalea covered in clusters of soft pink, fully double flowers from spring through fall rather than a single spring flush. Plant in moist, acidic, well-drained soil with at least five hours of direct sun daily, since heavier shade reduces the repeat flowering that makes this azalea distinctive. It is notably heat tolerant for an azalea and shows good resistance to deer and rabbit browsing once established. Water deeply during dry stretches and prune lightly right after the heaviest spring flush if shaping is needed.

common_name: Dragon Prince Cryptomeria (Dwarf Textured Japanese Cedar)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring in well-drained soil in full sun; the dense rounded habit needs no shearing and tolerates a wide range of soils.

directions: A true dwarf cryptomeria forming a tidy, rounded cushion of fine, stiff, light-green foliage that gives year-round texture without the bulk of standard Japanese cedar. Plant in well-drained soil in full sun; the naturally compact habit requires no pruning to keep its shape. It is notably heat and drought tolerant for a conifer and handles cold snaps well within its zone range, making it a reliable low-maintenance choice for foundation plantings, low hedges, or container specimens. Sold under Plant Development Services' Southern Living Plant Collection label, which carries this breeding program's 'Spg-3-0XX' internal selection codes.

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring in well-drained, sandy to average soil in full sun; the flattened, ground-hugging habit works well as an arborvitae groundcover.

directions: An unusually flat, ground-hugging arborvitae with layered sprays of foliage that stay under two feet tall while spreading two to three feet wide. Plant in well-drained soil, including sandy sites, in full sun; its sage-green summer color shifts to a striking blue-toned cast in winter. The dense, dwarf habit needs no pruning and works well softening the edges of hardscaping, filling gaps in gravel gardens, or forming a low textural drift at the front of a conifer bed.

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring in well-drained soil in full sun to part shade; water regularly through the first season to establish.

directions: A dense, rounded Hinoki falsecypress with bright yellow-gold outer foliage that bronzes attractively in winter while the innermost needles stay green, creating a layered two-tone effect. Plant in well-drained soil in full sun to part shade; it tolerates full sun without noticeable foliage burn, which is unusual for a gold conifer. The naturally polished mound shape rarely needs shearing. Mulch two to three inches and water deeply but less frequently once established to keep the root zone cool and evenly moist.

common_name: Coppertop Sweet Viburnum (Copper New-Growth Screening Viburnum)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in well-drained soil in full sun; drought resistant once established, making it useful in drought-prone regions.

directions: A fast, upright evergreen screening shrub whose new growth repeatedly emerges in brilliant dark maroon-to-copper tones before settling to dark green, giving season-long color after every flush. Plant in well-drained soil in full sun; fertilize in early spring with a slow-release fertilizer formulated for acid-loving plants. A light midsummer pruning triggers a second colorful flush of new leaves that lasts into late fall. Fragrant white spring flowers attract pollinators and are followed by small red fall berries, and the shrub is both deer resistant and largely free of significant pest or disease problems.

common_name: Forever Goldy Arborvitae (Slim Golden Columnar Western Redcedar)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring in well-drained soil in full sun; space tightly for a narrow screen or wider for a stand-alone accent.

directions: A slim, pyramidal western redcedar that holds bright golden foliage color even through full sun and summer heat, forming a narrow evergreen column well suited to tight spaces. Plant in well-drained soil in full sun; growth is moderate, typically twelve to eighteen inches per year once established. Space about two and a half to three feet apart on center for a tight continuous screen, or three and a half to four feet apart for individual accent specimens. The aromatic foliage is naturally resistant to deer and rabbit browsing, making it a reliable choice for waterwise, low-maintenance hedges and entry plantings.

planting.note: Start from pelleted seed or plugs indoors and transplant out around last frost; this series flowers one to two weeks earlier than comparable dianthus and does not require a heat treatment to initiate bloom.

directions: This F1 Sweet William selection produces raspberry-pink clustered blooms earlier in the season than most comparable dianthus, without needing supplemental heat treatment during production to trigger flowering. Start seed or plugs indoors and transplant out around the last frost date into full sun to light shade. Plug crop time runs about five to six weeks, with another six to eight weeks from transplant to finished flowering plants. Deadhead spent blooms to extend the flowering window into early summer.

common_name: WonderStar Pink Tomato (Pink Ribbed Compact Beefsteak Tomato)

planting.note: Start seed indoors 6-8 weeks before last frost and transplant once soil has warmed; this compact determinate variety suits small-space and container growing.

directions: A compact, early-maturing determinate tomato bred to produce large, oblate beefsteak-style fruit with an heirloom-style bright pink skin and ribbed shoulders, despite the plant's small container-friendly footprint. Transplant into full sun after soil has warmed, and support the upright 18-24 inch plants with a stake or small cage as fruit sets. Fruit average 8-10 ounces and roughly 2.5 by 3.5 inches, with good resistance to fusarium wilt, late blight, Septoria leaf spot, and verticillium wilt. Harvest at full color for the best sweet-tart flavor on sandwiches, in salads, or cooked.

common_name: KickStart Sweet Bell Pepper (Early Blocky Red Bell Pepper)

planting.note: Start seed indoors 8-10 weeks before last frost and transplant into warm soil after frost danger passes; fruit can be harvested green at 50-55 days or left to ripen fully red at 70-75 days.

directions: An early, high-yielding upright bell pepper producing medium-to-large, blocky fruit well suited to stuffing or chopping, with a sweet flavor at full ripeness. Transplant into full sun once the soil has warmed; the upright 20-30 inch plants hold fruit well off the ground. Expect green-stage harvest around 50-55 days from transplant or fully red fruit at 70-75 days, with individual peppers averaging 8-9 ounces. The variety carries resistance to multiple bacterial leaf spot strains, which helps reduce foliage loss in humid growing conditions.
